A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same actor–critic flow and retain the same main stability and convergence results. All 23 pages of each version, including equations and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds and proofs in the main text and Appendices A–C, without original experiments, simulations or data analyses.

after.justification: v2 likewise contains theoretical results rather than original empirical outcomes, including in Appendices A–E. Section 4's references to empirical success concern cited work.

M1.justification: The linear critic, MSBE semi-gradient update, mirror-descent actor and coupled continuous-time dynamics are retained. v2 reorganizes the update equations and discusses potentially taking multiple critic steps, but does not introduce a changed coupled procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions study the same theoretical class of infinite-horizon, entropy-regularised MDPs with general state and action spaces. Neither uses datasets or evaluates empirical tasks or scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed flow. Actor–critic and policy-gradient methods appear as related theoretical work; the additional citations do not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports empirical data splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets or testing procedures. The revisions to mathematical assumptions and limiting arguments are theoretical changes rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or case studies. Most results collected in v2's Appendix E are relocated theoretical corollaries, not newly conducted supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: Repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars and significance tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical result entries, numerical experimental outcomes or performance rankings. Changes to analytical examples and limiting statements are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: The main stability and convergence theorems and their proofs are retained after matching relocated material. v2 corrects Assumption 4.1's quantifier order, restricts the bounded Q-function definition to admissible policies, and adds limiting arguments in Remarks 2.1 and E.1. It removes v1's explicit square-root timescale example and associated 1/sqrt(t) statement following Corollary 6.1. These are localized theoretical revisions.

C1.justification: The title and contribution question explicitly focus on an actor–critic gradient flow. The abstract changes its convergence target from the optimal policy to the optimal regularised value function and emphasizes preventing finite-time blow-up. The central stability and convergence contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 expands the explanation of unbounded relative entropy and initialization difficulties, adds a forcing-and-damping interpretation of critic stability, and interprets small discount factors through the effective horizon. Remark E.1 adds a proposed strong-regularisation limit toward the reference policy. Section 7's limitations concerning continuous time, linear approximation and exact integration remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies an executable implementation, empirical hyperparameters, hardware information or code/data access instructions. The added details concern mathematical formulation and explanation rather than implementation or experimental reproducibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Bertsekas–Shreve and Hernández-Lerma–Lasserre textbooks and representation-related applications by Ma et al. and Ren et al., while removing Leahy et al. (2022). The central positioning relative to existing actor–critic convergence theory remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: occupancy definitions, dynamic programming and performance-difference material move to Appendix A; small-discount corollaries and proofs are collected in Appendix E; acknowledgements and references move after the appendices. The abstract and motivation are expanded, and Section 6 more explicitly organizes the steps toward the main theorem.

P2.justification: Neither version contains figures or tables. v2 groups the exact critic and actor updates into one displayed system, changes reference formatting and reflows the relocated material. The single-column design remains, although the longer running title crowds page numbers on odd-numbered pages.

improvement.justification: v2 improves organization, narrows the abstract's convergence claim and corrects the realisability quantifiers. However, new Section 1.2 asserts KL <= log|A| for arbitrary full-support reference measures, a bound requiring a uniform reference, while Remark E.1 chooses eta_0 = tau + epsilon without generally satisfying Theorem 5.1's eta_0 > tau/Gamma condition. With the main proofs essentially unchanged, clearer exposition coexists with inaccuracies in the added reasoning, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
